repositories.name: metadata-graph
repositories.reason: Owns the context graph: must add per-column classification to the model/store, suggest it from source tags on schema discovery, expose set/override and read via metadata-graph-api, and include it in metadata.dataset.changed.v1.

repositories.name: platform-contracts
repositories.reason: Source of truth for event JSON Schemas and OpenAPI specs; the ingestion.schema.discovered.v1 and metadata.dataset.changed.v1 schemas and the metadata-graph, entitlements and query-gateway OpenAPI specs need additive changes.

repositories.name: platform-sdk
repositories.reason: Shared typed REST clients (MetadataClient, entitlements client) and event helpers must model the new classification fields, the classification-override endpoint and masked_columns in access decisions.

repositories.name: ingestion-service
repositories.reason: Discovers source schemas and produces ingestion.schema.discovered.v1, which today carries only name/type/nullable per column, so it must additionally emit source column tags/comments for the suggestion (AC1).

repositories.name: entitlements-service
repositories.reason: Answers access decisions; must return which columns to mask when the requester lacks a pii:read grant, using column classifications from metadata.dataset.changed.v1 / metadata-graph-api (AC3).

repositories.name: query-gateway
repositories.reason: Serves query results to data consumers and already calls entitlements-api, so it must apply the masked_columns from the access decision to result sets (AC4).

repositories.name: dq-engine
repositories.reason: Runs data-quality rules and already reads metadata-graph-api, so it must look up column classifications and apply PII-format validation rules to PII columns (AC5).

repositories.name: platform-e2e
repositories.reason: Cross-service end-to-end suite covering ingestion, metadata-graph, entitlements, query-gateway and dq-engine; needs new scenarios for the classification-to-masking and PII-DQ flows plus a backward-compatibility run.

repositories.name: search-indexer
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 and validates against platform-contracts directly (not via platform-sdk), so it must be re-tested to confirm it tolerates the new optional column fields.

repositories.name: lineage-service
repositories.reason: Consumes metadata.dataset.changed.v1 (via platform-sdk), so it must be re-tested against the additive event payload and the SDK upgrade.

repositories.name: notification-service
repositories.reason: Calls metadata-graph-api through platform-sdk, so it must be re-tested against the additive column response and the new SDK version.

repositories.name: platform-catalog
repositories.reason: No new integration edge is required, but entries must be re-checked and corrected in the same PRs (e.g. metadata-graph pins platform-contracts directly but its catalog entry lists only platform-sdk).

considered_not_impacted.name: usage-metering
considered_not_impacted.reason: Only consumes gateway.access.logged.v1, whose shape this plan does not change.

considered_not_impacted.name: reporting-service
considered_not_impacted.reason: Decommissioned and archived per the catalog, even though the metadata-graph README still lists it as an event consumer.

dependencies.contract: entitlements-api access-decision endpoint (METHOD /path not visible in workspace)
entitlements-api access-decision endpoint (METHOD /path not visible in workspace)

contracts.name: ingestion.schema.discovered.v1
contracts.description: Add optional per-column `tags` (array of lower-case strings parsed from source column tags/comments, e.g. ['pii','email']) and optional raw `comment`; existing fields unchanged.

contracts.name: metadata.dataset.changed.v1
contracts.description: Add optional `classification` (PUBLIC|INTERNAL|CONFIDENTIAL|PII or null when unclassified) and `classification_source` (SUGGESTED|STEWARD) to each dataset.columns[] entry; classification changes are published with the existing change_type COLUMNS_CHANGED (no new enum value).

contracts.name: GET /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns
contracts.description: Each column gains optional `classification`, `classification_source`, `suggested_classification`, `classified_by` and `classified_at` fields.

contracts.name: PUT /v1/datasets/{urn}/columns/{column}/classification
contracts.description: New steward endpoint to set or override a column classification (body: classification, optional reason); persists with source STEWARD, returns the updated column and publishes metadata.dataset.changed.v1.

contracts.name: entitlements-api access-decision endpoint (METHOD /path not visible in workspace)
contracts.description: Decision response gains `masked_columns` (array of column names, empty when the principal holds pii:read or no PII columns) and optional `masking_reason`; allow/deny semantics unchanged.

contracts.name: query-api query-results endpoint (METHOD /path not visible in workspace)
contracts.description: Values of columns listed in masked_columns are replaced with a type-safe mask (null or fixed redaction token for strings) and the response gains optional `masked_columns` metadata; result schema/column order unchanged.

open_questions: Does ingestion-service already capture source column comments/tags internally, and what tag syntax do connectors expose beyond `tags: pii,email` (e.g. Hive TBLPROPERTIES, Postgres COMMENT, Snowflake tags)?
What is the tag-to-classification mapping (e.g. pii,email,phone,ssn -> PII; confidential -> CONFIDENTIAL; public -> PUBLIC) and the default for untagged columns: null/unclassified or INTERNAL?
Should unclassified columns be treated as unmasked (fail-open, non-breaking) or masked (fail-closed) once enforcement is enabled?

Do event schemas in platform-contracts set additionalProperties:false, and do search-indexer/lineage-service/entitlements-service validate strictly? This decides whether consumers must upgrade platform-contracts before metadata-graph emits the new fields.
Who authorizes the steward PUT classification endpoint (metadata-graph has no auth in the visible code): a new steward role in entitlements-service, or an existing gateway/IdP check?
Does entitlements-service already support a `pii:read` grant/scope, or must a new grant type and its management API be added?
Exact METHOD /path of the entitlements access-decision endpoint and the query-api results endpoint (OpenAPI files under platform-contracts/openapi/ are not in this workspace).
Masking strategy per data type (null vs redaction token vs partial/hashed) and whether consumers relying on non-null values in NOT NULL columns will break.

How does query-gateway map result columns of derived queries (joins, aliases, expressions) back to source dataset columns? Column-level lineage does not appear to exist (lineage-service is dataset-level).
Should gateway.access.logged.v1 record masked columns for audit? If yes it is an additive change and usage-metering becomes verify_only.
Which PII-format rules apply per PII subtype (email, phone, SSN, ...), and should results be published on dq.result.published.v1 with a rule category (additive) or reuse existing fields?
Should search-indexer index classification for faceted search (optional enhancement, not required by the ticket)?
Should classification be versioned/audited in the graph (history of steward overrides) for governance?
